episodes.202619: Tropical Storm Chantal developed along a frontal boundary off the Georgia coast before moving north making landfall at Litchfield Beach, SC at 4 AM EDT.
episodes.202640: A shortwave moving across the area triggered thunderstorm development across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska the afternoon of July 6. Storms produced both strong winds and damaging hail with a brief landspout ground circulation reported.
episodes.202641: A shortwave moving across the area triggered thunderstorm development across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska the afternoon of July 6. Storms produced both strong winds and damaging hail with a brief landspout ground circulation reported.
episodes.202669: Isolated severe thunderstorms over the Denver area and northeast Colorado plains. Video of a landspout tornado was taken by storm chasers. No damage was reported from the tornado or any other severe weather.
episodes.202767: A slow-moving cold front interacting with a moderately unstable but weakly sheared environment triggered clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms primarily along and south of a Paris to Taylorville line during the afternoon of July 6th.  A couple of the cells produced wind gusts of around 60mph, resulting in isolated wind damage in parts of Coles and Shelby counties.
episodes.202804: The monsoon high over northern Mexico built north into the desert southwest on July 6th and 7th. Daytime heating and moisture resulted in the development of scattered showers and storms across the northern and central mountains during the afternoon hours spreading east to lower elevations during the evening hours before tapering off shortly after sunset. Heavy rainfall from storms over the burn scars surrounding Ruidoso resulted in flash flooding on and downstream of the burn scars on July 6th followed by two separate rounds on July 7th with first round occurring during the early afternoon hours and the second round occurring during the mid evening hours just before sunset.
episodes.202828: As the far outer bands of tropical storm Chantal began to overspread portions of Eastern North Carolina, several rounds of isolated to widely scattered shower and thunderstorm activity impacted the region during the afternoon hours of July sixth. A few isolated storms became strong in nature bringing a threat for strong wind gusts to portions of the Crystal Coast.
episodes.202948: Several rounds of heavy rain fell ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon and evening on Saturday (7/05) with 2 to 3 inches of rain in a short time, causing flash flooding on the west side of Green Bay.
episodes.203304: A low pressure system that slowly moved east across the state produced convective showers and thunderstorms. Most of the favorable thermodynamic environment stayed off to the east of the region, with a few strong to severe storms clipping Fergus County. The primary hazard was severe wind gusts.
episodes.203821: Isolated thunderstorms produced heavy rain and localized flooding during the afternoon of July 6th.
episodes.203888: Thunderstorms moving through the Detroit River and Lake St. Clair produced wind gusts up around 40 knots.
episodes.204254: Numerous thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front during the late morning into early afternoon of July 6th. The high moisture/low shear environment was favorable for wet microbursts and heavy rainfall. Thunderstorms acted as expected given the environment, and wet microbursts produced isolated wind damage in central and east-central Missouri.
episodes.204255: Numerous thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front during the late morning into early afternoon of July 6th. The high moisture/low shear environment was favorable for wet microbursts and heavy rainfall. Thunderstorms generally acted as expected given the environment, with wind damage and flash flooding occurring. A tornado also impacted western Fayette County in the late afternoon.
episodes.204392: Sea breeze storms over a moist airmass with weak storm motion produced locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.204421: Thunderstorms developed across portions of the area during the afternoon hours of the 6th where golf ball to three inch diameter hail was reported in Norton county. Additional hail and wind reports were recorded in Rawlins, Thomas, Logan and Graham counties.
episodes.204432: On the afternoon of the fifth, scattered thunderstorms developed near the Raton Mesa of New Mexico and propagated to the southeast through the evening hours. This activity grew upscale late in the evening as it approached the Texas/New Mexico state line and was able to take advantage of modest instability. As the complex of storms crossed into the southwestern Texas Panhandle, a severe wind gust was recorded near Friona (Parmer County).
episodes.204671: Tropical Storm Chantal made landfall over northeastern South Carolina during the morning hours of July 6. The remnants of Chantal then tracked west-northwest into portions of central North Carolina, stalling out over the area before tracking east-northeast into Virginia by the 7th of July. Catastrophic flash flooding occurred from record rainfall of up to 11 inches in some spots of the Piedmont, included 6 flash flood fatalities across Chatham, Alamance, and Orange Counties. Widespread flooding particularly affected the counties of Orange, Chatman, and Moore. Four EF-1 tornadoes also touched down over portions Lee, Chatham, Alamance, and Orange Counties. Preliminary loss estimates across central North Carolina exceeded 40 million.
episodes.204987: On the afternoon of July 6, 2025, a weak vorticity maximum moving east from Colorado into Nebraska initiated a mesoscale convective system across eastern Nebraska. The system produced several strong wind gusts before gradually weakening as it progressed eastward toward the Missouri River. A public mesonet station reported a peak wind gust of 64 mph east of Cedar Rapids, NE.
episodes.205004: A persistent mid-level anticyclonic circulation remained over Texas and generated thunderstorms over South-Central Texas. Some of these storms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.205219: Heavy rainfall and isolated strong storms impacted portions of southeast Arkansas.
episodes.205429: With a moist airmass in place over the region, afternoon pulse thunderstorms developed across southwestern Missouri producing localized wind damage and flooding. Significant flooding occurred in eastern Greene County where between 3 and 6 inches of rain fall over a less than 6 hour period as persistent slow moving storms developed over the county. During the period, some locations saw in excess of an inch of rain in a 15 minute period.
episodes.205533: Isolated thunderstorms developed across portions of south-central and southeast Kansas during the early afternoon hours of July 6th. Thunderstorm coverage became more-numerous during the mid to late afternoon hours across south-central Kansas. These particular storms produced severe caliber hail and damaging winds.
episodes.205538: Late morning convection within deep layer southwest flow over the state south of Tropical Depression Chantal centered just inland near the border of the Carolinas produces a waterspout offshore Osprey in Sarasota County.
episodes.205632: Cold front moved into Maine from the northwest. Warm sector ahead of aforementioned cold front, along with plenty of moisture, led to a warm, humid day, along with plentiful instability, that resulted in convection in Piscataquis and Penobscot counties. Storm originally developed in Quebec / western Maine, and began to strengthen in Piscataquis county. Storms eventually weakened and continued to move east into New Brunswick. Caused some wind damage along Telos Road in Piscataquis, knocking down 4 healthy trees. Some more thunderstorms developed in southern Penobscot, later in the afternoon, resulting in knocked trees and various lightning strikes. These storms eventually weakened and moved offshore.
episodes.205638: A weakness aloft moved across the region during early July. A couple isolated severe storms resulted.
episodes.205687: From the July 4th weekend into the early part of the following week, a weak upper trough lingered over North and Central Texas, triggering several days of scattered showers and thunderstorms. A saturated atmosphere combined with slow storm motions resulted in numerous flash flooding events throughout the region, particularly in Central Texas.
episodes.205775: Severe thunderstorms occurred for a second day in a row. In Sublette County, a trained spotter reported golf ball size hail north of Cora. A second round of severe thunderstorms occurred in the evening, with wind gusts of 66 mph at the Rock Springs aiport and gusts as high as 61 mph near Casper.
episodes.205938: Storms developed over the Black Hills and quickly formed into a line of storms. This squall line went on to produce widespread severe wind gusts across much of the county warning area.
episodes.205940: A few thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening and produced minor wind damage and quarter size hail reports.
episodes.205995: Clusters of slow moving thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts and heavy rainfall across eastern Wyoming.
episodes.206033: On the evening of July 5th, an upper level disturbance took advantage of a highly moist and unstable environment to generate a line of thunderstorms across the western Panhandles. These storms went on to produce sub-severe hail and several severe wind gusts and wind damage.
episodes.206063: In the late afternoon and early evening of the 5th, a line of storms developed across eastern Colorado and proceeded to the east-southeast. The bulk of the line was not severe, but intense sections of the line formed on the northern and southern edges, leading to 50-56 MPH gusts on the northern edge and gusts up to 63 MPH in the southern section.
episodes.206081: In the late afternoon and early evening of the 5th, a line of storms developed across eastern Colorado and proceeded to the east-southeast. Gusts ranging from 60 to 72 MPH were recorded, as was penny size hail.
episodes.206105: Slow moving thunderstorms formed over Benson, AZ that produced heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding. Over the 2 hours that rainfall fell, two rainfall gauges reported 1.10-1.25 inches of rainfall. Two separate sections of Pomerene Rd had flooding that made the roadway impassable.
episodes.206189: Scattered thunderstorms developed over coastal waters and inland lakes on July 6, 2025. A gust of 39 mph (34 kt) was measured at the Pontchartrain Causeway during a thunderstorm over Lake Pontchartrain. Later in the afternoon, boaters observed two waterspouts between Bayou Caddy and Half Moon Island in the Mississippi Sound.
episodes.206306: Two supercells that developed along the higher terrain pushed across El Paso County due to westerly flow aloft. Both supercells would go on to produce swaths of severe hail across central El Paso County.
episodes.206320: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Treasure Coast.
episodes.206349: Strong thunderstorms developed around the Atlantic coast of Southeast Florida and Lake Okeechobee on the afternoon of July 6, 2025 as a mid level disturbance passed to the northwest of the region and surface boundary over northern portions of the state retreated northward.
episodes.206376: Thunderstorms occurred across much of southern Montana, producing gusts up to 70 mph and hail up to 1.75 inches in diameter.

Heavy rain from slow moving storms on the South Fork and McBride burn scars resulted in flash flooding on and downstream of the burn scars. Several roads along and crossing the Rio Ruidoso were closed due to the resultant flash flooding and debris flow in the river. This included Mechem Drive, Ebarb Drive at Main Road and West Redwood Road, Fern Trail at Terrance and Grindstone, Eagle Bridge on Eagle Road, Gavilan Bridge on Gavilan Canyon Road in Hollywood, Cree Meadows at Country Club and Heath, Robin Road, Hull Road, and Paradise Canyon Road. The floodwaters and debris flow washed away a vehicle on Porr Drive. No information was known on if any occupants were in the vehicle at the time. Another vehicle was stuck in flood waters at Apache Hills Drive and Grant Drive. Finally, 2 to 3 inches of water entered a home on Ash Drive.
The public reported an impassable roadway with rapidly-flowing water covering US 15-501 in Southern Pines.

An EF-1 tornado touched down at the Raleigh Executive Jetport 7.5 miles northeast of Sanford in Lee County, North Carolina. Several hangers had damage to wall panels and doors. Several aircraft were damaged. Minor damage to the taxiway occurred. The tornado briefly lifted before touching back down near its end point, and resulted in minor damage to several mobile homes and several trees that were snapped and uprooted.
